chunks: And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a Dhimmiyyah (non-Muslim woman under protection) while already married to a Muslim woman, he said: "They are separated, and one-eighth of the hadd punishment is inflicted, which is twelve and a half lashes. If the Muslim woman consents, one-eighth of the punishment is inflicted, and they are not separated." I asked: "How is half a lash inflicted?" He said: "The whip is held by its middle, and he is struck with it."

key_terms.السَّوْطُ: A whip used for corporal punishment
key_terms.ثُمُنَ الْحَدِّ: One-eighth of the prescribed corporal punishment
key_terms.ذِمِّيَّةٌ: A non-Muslim woman living under Muslim protection

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling and punishment for a Muslim man who marries a non-Muslim woman while already married to a Muslim woman?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (as) establishes that a man marrying a Kitabi (non-Muslim) woman while already married to a Muslim incurs a partial corporal punishment of twelve and a half lashes, with separation from the non-Muslim wife being the default ruling. However, if the Muslim wife consents to the polygyny, the separation is waived while the punishment remains, reflecting the juristic principle of prioritizing the consent of the primary wife in mixed-faith unions. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia approach to the compatibility of spouses in polygynous arrangements, emphasizing the status of the Muslim wife as a decisive factor.
